observations: The total number of participants with a scan was 85, with 12 censored.
99% of the patients in the intervention group received their scan within 29 days.
Scans in the usual care group were performed steadily over a longer time period.
The mean HR for the new model of care was 16.1, 95% CI 9.1 to 29.2.
The median reduction in time to scan was close to 1 year (mean reduction 0.92 years, 95% CI 0.56 to 1.45).
question: How did the time to scan differ between the intervention group and the usual care group?

interpretation: The intervention group had a significantly shorter time to scan compared to the usual care group.
interpretation_limits: The comparison was made between the intervention group and the usual care group within the study's specific conditions.
cautions: The results are specific to the conditions and population studied and may not be generalizable to other settings.
suggested_next_steps: Conduct follow-up experiments to compare the time to scan under different healthcare settings or populations.

can_conclude: The intervention group had a shorter time to scan compared to the usual care group.
cannot_conclude: ANY molecular, structural, catalytic, physiological, or clinical explanations.
ANY causal or mechanistic claims not explicitly demonstrated.
